detail.reason: Customer reported two product issues: voice agent transfers arriving without notes, and dynamic number insertion broken on React order pages; plus a Google Sheets reporting feature request.

assignments.name: AI agent context lost on Genesys transfers
Dynamic number insertion fails after first page load

decisions.reason: matched rule "Other feature requests → Core product" (priority 62)

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], like, [PERSON_3]. Thanks for making time this afternoon. How's the week going out there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Pretty good. Busy. Harvest is in full swing, so half the office is either talking about beans or trying to get out of the office to go look at beans.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: My brother started combining Tuesday. He sent me a picture at like six in the morning. I don't know what he wanted me to do about it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, my in-laws farm over by Hartford, so we're on standby for babysitting while they run.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That's the season. Okay, I've got us down for the quarterly review. I pulled the numbers for July through September. Want me to just walk through what I'm seeing, and you all jump in whenever?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: So call volume across tracking numbers was up about eleven percent quarter over quarter, which tracks with the new order flow going live in September.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Google Ads drove most of that. The one thing that stands out to me is the last week of September.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The outage.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: The outage. September twenty-ninth, right? I saw the spike. What did that look like from your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So that that was a fiber cut over by the state line, took down a chunk of the network for most of the day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Our care queue normally runs maybe sixty, seventy calls a day. That day it was, I don't know, north of two thousand.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: It was a lot. Our status page got hammered too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: During the outage on the twenty-ninth the voice agent took thousands of calls, which was great, but every one it passed to my team came over with no notes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: No notes. So the caller talks to the agent, the agent decides it needs a person, transfers, and the rep picks up with nothing on the screen?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nothing. No name, no account, no idea what they already said. So my reps are starting over from scratch with somebody who's already been on hold for ten minutes and is not happy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: How many of those transfers are we talking about that day?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'd have to pull it, but but a few hundred at least. The ones that stayed with the agent were fine, honestly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It was the handoffs that hurt.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. Let me write that down and take it back to the team. Can you get me one or two call IDs from that day so I can hand over actual examples?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I can pull a couple this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That's perfect. And you know, just so I'm clear, this is specifically the transfer into your contact center, not the agent's own calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. The agent itself did its job. It's the handoff.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Got it. Okay, [PERSON_3], you wanted to talk about the order flow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah. So we rebuilt the whole thing as a single-page app, React, launched the second week of September. Generally it's been good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Faster, fewer drop-offs. But we noticed something in the tracking pretty quick.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: What's that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: the number swap stopped working on our order pages after we moved to the new React app

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: The dynamic number insertion.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah. On the marketing site it's fine, numbers swap like they always did. But once you're inside the order flow, it's the static number.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So any call from that page attributes to the wrong thing, or to nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Which matters because that's exactly where people call from. They get three steps in, something doesn't validate, they pick up the phone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: How long has it been like that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Since launch. We caught it maybe two weeks in. I assumed it was on our end, some lifecycle thing um, with the tag not firing on route changes, but I poked at it and couldn't pin it down.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. So one, the tag needs to fire on route change, not just initial page load. Two, there may be something about how the number pool is being read in that context.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I I don't want to guess at it on the call. Can I get the URL pattern for one of those order pages, and roughly when the two weeks in was?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll send you a staging link and a prod link. Both reproduce.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Good. I'll get that in front of support today so it's not sitting over the weekend.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: [PERSON_1], you had a a reporting thing on the list too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah. So every Monday I pull the weekly source report, by campaign, by channel, and I paste it into a deck for our VP and the regional managers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's not hard, it's just... every Monday, same thing. I mean, Download the CSV, clean it it up, um, paste it in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: How long does that take you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Twenty minutes if nothing's weird. Forty if something's weird. And it's me doing it, which means if I'm traveling it doesn't happen.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And where does it end up?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Google Sheets. That's where the the deck pulls from. I'd love a way to get the weekly source report into Google Sheets without someone downloading it

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: So a scheduled push, or a live connection, straight into a sheet.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Either. I just don't want a um, human in the loop on a Tuesday morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. I'll take that one back too. I know we talked about it briefly in July, so let me see where it sits.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Anything else on the list before I run through the the rest of the metrics?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, I think that's the two.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. So the rest is pretty quiet. Call tracking attribution is holding steady, Google Ads conversions are flowing, Marketo's getting what it needs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Anything on your end feeling off there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that side's fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Good. And the agent's handling routine outage calls the way you wanted?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that part's working. People get the status message, so, they get the ETA, most of them hang up happy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Good. You're at sixty seats, still, right?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Uh, Sixty-one as of last month. One new hire in care.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll note that. Renewal's October of next year, so we've got plenty of runway, but if the seat count keeps creeping I'd rather know early.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Probably one or two more before spring. Nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. Let me get through the rest and then we can get you out of here.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Before you do, is the football game still on for tonight? I heard they moved it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Moved to seven. Homecoming, so they wanted the lights.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Oh, that's why. My nephew's on the line, he's been talking about it all week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Who are they playing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: The team from over in Mitchell. Should be a good one. They're undefeated.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So are we.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: We're four and three.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: In conference.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll leave that one alone. Okay, so to wrap the numbers. Volume up eleven percent, uh, agent handled the outage traffic, attribution's clean outside the order flow issue.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I've got three things: call IDs from [PERSON_2], the staging and prod links from [PERSON_3], and the Google Sheets report for [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll send a follow-up today with those three items and who's on each. If the number swap thing comes back faster than I expect, I'll flag it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Anything you want me to add or take off before I write it up?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, that that covers it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, so, we're good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Great. Then go enjoy the game. Good luck tonight, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks. I'll be the one in the bad jacket.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: You always are.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Have a good weekend, everybody. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You too, [PERSON_4]. Thanks.
